pr_title: Split `ComputedVisibility` into two components to allow for accurate change detection and speed up visibility propagation
pr_comments: Could you run some benchmarks? I expect this to be quite performance sensitive, but I'd put even odds on improvements vs regressions.

From an architectural and usability perspective I really like these proposed changes. I am nervous about performance costs here: I often see these systems as among the most expensive in real applications.

I ran the stress test `cargo run --release --example many_foxes`:

1. Main - avg fps of 285.2 over 5239 frames.
2. This PR - avg FPS of 287.9 over 5475 frames.
With `cargo run --release --example bevymark` with ~8000 birds, the FPS stays in the high 600s with and without this PR. I don't think this PR adds or takes away performance.
Would it be possible to keep it as one component and check if the value changes before updating it? Or triggering change manually when needed?

> Would it be possible to keep it as one component and check if the value changes before updating it?

That's the "naive" solution I mentioned in #8267. In order for that approach to work, we'd have to overhaul how view visibility is calculated.

Each frame, the view visibility of every entity is reset. Then any number of systems belonging to the `CheckVisibility` set will mark entities that are visible in any view. Systems belonging to this set can live in any crate, not just `bevy_render`. View calculations are done in `bevy_pbr`, and are allowed to be performed in 3rd party. Because of this, it's not as simple as just using `set_if_neq`.

Furthermore, I think it is good to split it into separate components, even without the change detection issue. Inherited visibility and view visibility are separate concepts, and it's odd to bundle them the way we do now.
@DGriffin91 was running into performance issues with visibility, maybe they can test this?

Ran this vs bevy main on [many_kitchens_no_render](https://github.com/DGriffin91/bevy_scene_that_should_be_fast/tree/many_kitchens_no_render) without changing anything and it seems to run at about the same either way.  Looks like `visibility_propagate_system` is taking about 20ms per frame in this scene that doesn't modify visibility or render anything. Should I test something specific?

> I don't think this PR adds or takes away performance.

This was mentioned previously, so this result is expected then?

> Looks like `visibility_propagate_system` is taking about 20ms per frame in this scene that doesn't modify visibility or render anything.

Hmm. Previously, `visibility_propagate_system` didn't use change detection ~~(as it was broken). Now that I've fixed change detection~~, maybe I can squeeze some more performance out of this system by only propagating visibility when it changes.

I've rewritten `visibility_propagate_system` to only update visibility when it changes.

Running `many_foxes` on my macbook, I get
* Main - 13.25 average FPS.
* This branch - 14.2 average FPS.

@DGriffin91 can you try running your scene again?

Note that approach his has a pitfall, depending on the iteration order of a query. If an entity and its ancestor has their visibility modified in the same frame, and if the descendant entity gets yielded first, then the descendant may have its visibility propagated twice in the same frame. This issue will not happen if the ancestor entity is yielded first. The effects of duplicate propagations are mitigated by the fact that downward propagation is halted whenever an entity with unchanged inherited visibility is encountered, such as entities that are unconditionally visible or hidden.

I think this pitfall is preferable to the way it currently works, where the entire hierarchy of visibility entities is traversed every single frame, even when no entities have their visibility updated.

Tried this again. The overall frame time is similar between this and main (~51ms). For main I used a commit near when this last had bevy main merged into it, if I use latest bevy main then main is faster. 

However, the time in `visibility_propagate_system` has reduced drastically. It was previously 20ms and is now around 700us. Not sure if the overall frame time not going down is just because with parallelism all the time spent in `visibility_propagate_system` was also spent in other threads doing other things, or if there would now be more time spent elsewhere?

> Not sure if the overall frame time not going down is just because with parallelism all the time spent in `visibility_propagate_system` was also spent in other threads doing other things, or if there would now be more time spent elsewhere?

I don't see where any extra time would be spent, so parallelism is a pretty good guess. Is it there an improvement if you run it single-threaded?
@JoJoJet How do I run it single threaded?
You should be able to just disable the `multi-threaded` cargo feature for bevy.
Without the `multi-threaded` feature I get 101ms on bevy main and 86ms on this PR. Nice work!
Thanks for the review! I believe that's everything.

issue_context.title: `Changed<ComputedVisibility>` always evaluates as true
comments: This should be changed to use `PartialEq`-based change tracking, once we have it.

I tried a naive fix for this, and is seems like this bug is a consequence of how the "is visible in view" calculation is currently done. Each frame, the view visibility of every entity is reset inside of `visibility_propagate_system`, and then later on `check_visibility` flags each entity that is visible to any camera. In order to fix this we'll have to carefully consider how these two systems interact with one another to avoid marking unnecessary changes.

review_comments: Non-blocking: this may benefit from parallel query iteration: it's a trivial loop with a ton of entities in it.

I ran `cargo run --release --example many_foxes`

1. Without par_iter: avg fps 288.0 over 5285 frames.
2. With par_iter: avg fps 281.8 over 5073.

Parallel iteration doesn't seem to have much of an effect, though it's possible that it would scale better for scenes with a huge number of entities.

Given that we have a trivial getter, and a public way to set values as both true and false, I have a hard time seeing why we shouldn't just make this field pub.

The docs about how to use this are excellent, but they could just be moved to the struct level.

In previous discussion about components like `Parent`, I think it was decided that we should avoid the `.0` syntax in public APIs, which is why I opted to derive deref and add a getter.

I decided not to provide a `.set(false)` option, as marking an entity as visible in view is meant to be irreversible during a given frame (this is a property I carried over from the old API, which had `.set_visible_in_view()`). Of course you could still reset the view visibility by just overwriting the entire component, but at least this API nudges users in the right direction.

Agreed about the documentation.
